questions.q: What does an interface in TypeScript define?
options: A runtime class with methods
The required shape of an object — its property names and their types
A compiled JavaScript function
A database schema enforced at runtime
questions.explain: An interface is a compile-time description of an object's shape: what properties it must have and what type each one is.

questions.q: In interface Wallet { address: string; nickname?: string; }, what does the ? after nickname mean?
options: nickname must always be a string of length greater than zero
nickname is optional and can be omitted entirely
nickname can never be reassigned
nickname is a typo and will cause an error
questions.explain: A ? after a property name marks it optional — an object satisfying the interface doesn't have to include it.

questions.q: What can a type alias express that an interface cannot?
options: Object shapes with required properties
A union of specific allowed values, like "pending" | "confirmed" | "failed"
Properties with a string type
Nothing — they are functionally identical in every case
questions.explain: type aliases can describe unions, primitives, and tuples; interface is limited to describing object (and function/class) shapes.

questions.q: What happens when you declare the same interface name twice with different members?
options: A compiler error: duplicate identifier
TypeScript merges the members from both declarations into one
Only the second declaration is used; the first is discarded
It's allowed but produces a runtime warning
questions.explain: Declaration merging combines multiple interface declarations of the same name into a single merged shape — type aliases don't support this and raise a duplicate-identifier error instead.

questions.q: What does marking a property readonly in an interface do?
options: Prevents the property from ever being read
Allows the property to be read freely but blocks reassigning it after the object is created
Makes the property optional
Converts the property to a constant at compile time with no other effect on usage
questions.explain: readonly properties can still be read normally, but TypeScript flags any attempt to assign a new value to them after the object's initial creation.
